# Ridu 0.19.0

Collections and globals that already store documents can now turn on versions. On Windows, SQLite
projects start, the admin loads, `ridu migrate create` succeeds, and Ctrl+C stops every process
`ridu dev` started.

## Changes

- Setting `Versions: true` on an existing collection or global no longer fails with
  `RIDU_VERSIONS_ENABLE_UNSUPPORTED`. A migration records what the documents it already stores
  become:
  - `published`: each document is published with a first version and a matching draft, so readers
    keep seeing it.
  - `draft`: each document stays an unpublished draft with a first version, and public reads stop
    returning it until it is published. This needs drafts.
  - `require-empty`: `ridu migrate up` stops while the collection stores any document.

  `ridu migrate create` takes the choice from `--versions-existing` or asks in a terminal.
  `ridu dev` enables versions without asking while the collection stores nothing. Otherwise it asks
  published, draft or cancel, then writes and applies the migration like an accepted rename. SQLite,
  PostgreSQL and MongoDB apply the choice in the migration's transaction, and `ridu migrate verify`
  replays it. See [Enabling versions](https://riducms.com/docs/migrations/enable-versions/).

## Fixes

- On Windows, every command that opened a SQLite file by path failed with
  `parse SQLite path: … invalid port`, including `ridu dev`, `ridu migrate plan`, `up` and `verify`,
  and the server. Paths now become `file:///C:/…` URIs, and UNC shares work too.
- On Windows, the admin never loaded under `ridu dev`: no `@admin/` import resolved, because Vite's
  module IDs start with a drive. A Windows `ridu build` also split `@riducms/ui` into many small
  chunks.
- On Windows, `ridu migrate create` wrote the migration and then exited with "Access is denied", and
  the local storage adapter's health check, uploads and deletes failed the same way. Ridu no longer
  syncs directories on Windows, where the file system already makes those changes durable.
- On Windows, Ctrl+C on `ridu dev` left the admin's Vite processes running and holding port 5173.
  Each process `ridu dev` starts now runs in a job object that ends its whole tree when Ridu stops,
  even if Ridu itself is killed. Through the npm launcher, the first Ctrl+C lets Ridu shut down
  cleanly and a second ends it at once.

Windows remains a source-build target without release qualification.

## Breaking changes and upgrade

Update the Go module and all Ridu npm packages to 0.19.0 together, regenerate application contracts,
and rebuild the admin and application binary.

- `sqlite.CreateArtifact`, `postgres.CreateArtifact` and `postgres.BuildArtifact` take an
  `ArtifactOptions` value in place of positional renames, destructive approval and transforms, as
  `mongodb.CreateArtifact` already did. `sqlite.CreateArtifactWithRenames` is removed; pass
  `ArtifactOptions{Renames: …}`. The CLI commands are unchanged.
- Migration artifacts gain the `enable_versions` step kind. Planner versions are unchanged, so
  existing histories replay as before.
- On PostgreSQL and MongoDB, a migration that enables versions needs
  `ridu migrate up --allow-maintenance`.
- The generated SQLite server now accepts Windows `file:` URIs in `RIDU_SQLITE_PATH`. To use them
  in an existing project, copy `sqliteDatabasePath` from `cmd/server/main.go` in a new project.

This is a pre-1 release with breaking contracts; keep the coordinated packages aligned. Production
still runs as a Go binary with its static admin embedded, without a JavaScript server.
